elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: As rendered, 12.4 reads "Customer shall not develop, market, or sell any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory" — the "acquire" prong is deleted, so no purchase/requirements restriction remains on Customer. 12.3 affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom to acquire, license, or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and records that Customer "has made no exclusivity ... commitment." 7.2's disclose-and-match duty is a right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic: it conditions timing but does not prohibit engaging another provider once honoured, so under the stated rule boundary it is MFN, not exclusivity.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation survives the redline (the acquisition bar in 12.4 is deleted and 12.3 confirms no exclusivity commitment), so there is no exclusivity scope requiring category limitation.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: the residual 12.4 term-plus-24-month restriction covers only develop/market/sell competing products, not procurement from third parties; no purchasing exclusivity period exists to cap.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no exclusivity obligation remains, so no performance-based exit is required.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no exclusivity obligation remains, so no delivery-failure exit is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole preferred element is met because the only operative sole-supplier mechanic (the "or acquire" prong of 12.4) is struck, leaving Customer free to procure competing products or services from any third party, consistent with 12.3.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because, with no exclusivity surviving, there is no scope, duration, or exit mechanic to specify; the preferred outcome is a fortiori stronger.

Minimality holds: the edit removes exactly one word ("acquire") plus the resulting comma, retains the Customer-favourable 12.3 disclaimer, retains the develop/market/sell non-compete prong (outside this checklist), and adds no new obligation, procedure, or boilerplate.

Intent is preserved: timing, territory, and the term-plus-24-month tail of 12.4 survive intact; 7.2's disclose-and-match mechanic is untouched and correctly routed to MFN rather than double-flagged here; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Note (not a defect of this redline): the residual 12.4 develop/market/sell prong still sits in tension with 12.3's statement that Customer has made "no ... non-compete" commitment. That conflict pre-exists the edit and falls under a restrictive-covenant/non-compete rule rather than EXCLUSIVITY; if the team wants it resolved, it should be raised there rather than by expanding this redline.
